exposure: cesarean delivery with and without uterine artery embolization (UAE) for the management of placenta accreta spectrum disorder
Uterine artery embolization (UAE) during cesarean delivery
cohort: 272 pregnant women with placenta accreta spectrum disorder who underwent cesarean delivery (64 with UAE, 208 without UAE)
finding: While associated with longer operative times, higher blood loss, and more postoperative complications, cesarean delivery with UAE for placenta accreta spectrum disorder was associated with a lower hysterectomy rate and comparable long-term obstetrical outcomes compared to cesarean delivery without UAE.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery using uterine artery embolization in placenta accreta spectrum disorder is associated with a higher rate of operative and postoperative complications, but reduces the need for hysterectomy.
